Read on drafting, and read again on review.** The `paper-authoring`\n4\tskill and the `prose-reviewer` agent both consume this file, so a rule cannot mean one\n5\tthing while writing and another while reviewing.\n6\t\n7\t⚠️ **This is the shared FLOOR, not the whole review.** The reviewer additionally carries\n8\treader-outcome questions that do not appear here and that an author must never be given as\n9\ta checklist: a generator optimises against any list it can see. The em-dash: prohibited outright, including in headings\n18\t\n19\t**Never write `---` or a literal `—`.** Two forms exist and both are banned.\n20\t\n21\t**Why this one is absolute.** An em-dash reads as machine-authored to a 2026 reader and\n22\tcosts trust before the physics is evaluated. One is as disqualifying as forty, so there is\n23\tno acceptable density. Enforced by `validate.py --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free`, target\n24\tzero. Measured before the corpus was swept: **741 of them, and 0 of 21 bundles clean.**\n25\t\n26\t### ⚠️ The en-dash `--` is MANDATORY and must never be touched\n27\t\n28\t`--` (exactly two hyphens) is a different character doing a different job, and the corpus\n29\tcarries **1,121** of them:\n30\t\n31\t- compound eponyms: `Bose--Einstein`, `Bekenstein--Hawking`, `Schwinger--Keldysh`,\n32\t  `Kaul--Majumdar`, `Chowdhury--Hartnoll--Hebbar--Khondaker`, `SK--EFT`\n33\t- numeric ranges: `pp. 10--15`, `$2$--$3$ K`\n34\t\n35\t**An author over-correcting to \"no dashes at all\" breaks every compound name in the\n36\tprogram, and the check cannot see it** because it counts exactly three hyphens. This is the\n37\tsingle highest-cost mistake available here. One live line contained both:\n38\t`observables---also drives the SK--EFT`.\n39\t\n40\tA third variant exists in the wild: the literal Unicode en-dash `–` (U+2013), found as\n41\t`Kaul–Majumdar` and `Chowdhury–Hartnoll–Hebbar–Khondaker`. Write `--` instead; D3 once\n42\tspelled the same name both ways.\n43\t\n44\t### Replacing an em-dash is a REWRITE, not a substitution\n45\t\n46\tA mechanical swap produces comma splices. Identify the job the dash was doing, then use the\n47\tpunctuation that already exists for that job. Frequencies below are from six independent\n48\treadings of all 741 occurrences.\n49\t\n50\t| The dash was doing | Frequency | Write instead |\n51\t|---|---|---|\n52\t| Paired aside interrupting a clause | ~45–55% | parentheses; a comma pair when the aside is short and contains no commas of its own |\n53\t| Introducing an explanation, expansion or list | ~30–45% | a colon |\n54\t| Separating a label from its gloss in `\\item`, `\\subsection{}`, `\\paragraph{}` | ~15% | a colon, always |\n55\t| Contrastive \"X, not Y\" interjection | ~7% | a comma pair (parentheses would demote a correction to an aside) |\n56\t| Joining two independent clauses | ~3–15% | a semicolon, or a full stop and a new sentence |\n57\t| Trailing appositive glossing a number's significance | common in E1/E2 | a comma |\n58\t\n59\t### The four hard cases, each of which defeats a mechanical fix\n60\t\n61\t1. **The aside contains its own parenthetical or citation.** Converting the outer dash to\n62\t   parentheses yields stacked or nested parens that read as a stutter:\n63\t   `(\\lean{diamondDist_eq_choiSDP}) (the Watrous semidefinite program~\\cite{Watrous2018}) is proven`.\n64\t   **Merge the tag and the aside into ONE parenthetical** with an internal comma or\n65\t   semicolon. Do not nest.\n66\t2. **The aside contains a comma-separated list.** Comma-punctuating it makes the reader\n67\t   parse the inner items as continuing the outer sentence's list. Use parentheses.\n68\t3. **The sentence already has a colon later on.** Adding a second colon reads as a nested\n69\t   label. Restructure with a copula: `X is the headline theorem: Y`.\n70\t4. **Three levels of subordination.** An aside inside an aside inside a main clause is a\n71\t   sentence trying to be three sentences. Split it.\n72\t\n73\t### The generative habits behind them: prohibit these, not just the symbol\n74\t\n75\tAll six readers converged on the same root, so treat it as the rule that matters:\n76\t\n77\t> **Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification.** Write the clarification as\n78\t> its own sentence, before or after.\n79\t\n80\tThe dominant shape was *claim, dash, restatement-with-a-twist, dash, continuation*: draft a\n81\tclean declarative, then, worried a reader will misattribute a convention or miss a caveat,\n82\tsplice the qualifier into the middle. It concentrated in exactly the paragraphs doing the\n83\theaviest epistemic hedging (novelty disclaimers, provenance caveats, convention-pinning),\n84\twhich is where this project's prose is densest.\n85\t\n86\tFour more shapes, each of which reliably produces an em-dash:\n87\t\n88\t- **Name-then-gloss in itemised lists.** `\\item \\verb|foo_bar|: the substantive witness`.\n89\t  Use the colon from the start; this was the single most common pattern in the Lean-heavy\n90\t  bundles.\n91\t- **Label-then-gloss in headings.** `\\subsection{Pillar 1: Golterman--Shamir}`. A dash in a\n92\t  heading also reads as a tic when scanning the table of contents.\n93\t- **Tag-stacking.** A claim ending in a `\\lean{...}` identifier in parens, then a dash\n94\t  glossing that identifier. This is an appositive that got dash-punctuated only because the\n95\t  sentence had already spent its parentheses.\n96\t- **Claim-then-immediately-re-scope.** `T_H \\approx 2.4$ K --- nine orders of magnitude\n97\t  above atomic BEC --- with adiabaticity...`. A defensible instinct for a rigorous program,\n98\t  executed with the wrong punctuation: pick the syntax that matches the qualifier's\n99\t  grammatical role.\n100\t\n101\t---\n102\t\n103\t## 2. Banned forms:\n110\t\n111\t- a correction stamped with a date: `(corrected 2026-08-01)`\n112\t- an account of an earlier draft: `three earlier drafts of this paragraph asserted...`\n113\t- a first-person superseded claim: `We previously shipped a theorem asserting...`\n114\t- an internal review reference: `(D11 Stage-13 round-14 finding 6.2)`\n115\t- the project's own planning documents: `Our earlier planning documents described...`\n116\t- review rounds cast as actors: `rounds 7 and 10 both rated this cosmetic`\n117\t- a claim about the paper's own drafting: `typeset unconditionally in every draft`\n118\t\n119\t**The history is not lost, it moves.** `papers/<X>/change_log.md` and\n120\t`docs/review_finding_supersessions.json` are where a later reader can actually check it, and\n121\tthe ledger entry is required by the lift procedure anyway.\n122\t\n123\t### ⚠️ Removing narration is not deleting content\n124\t\n125\tMost of these passages wrap something real, and the substance must survive:\n126\t\n127\t- **A retraction is a scientific disclosure.** Restate it as a present-tense negative\n128\t  result: what is *not* claimed and why it fails. Do not delete the paragraph.\n129\t- **A scope correction states the correct scope.** Keep every factual statement about what\n130\t  a module does and does not contain, including file:line references. Drop only \"earlier\n131\t  drafts called it X\" and the date/round/finding tag.\n132\t- **A completeness disclaimer is a real caveat.** Keep it; drop the account of what two\n133\t  earlier drafts asserted.\n134\t\n135\t### What is NOT prohibited\n136\t\n137\tReporting that *the literature* corrected something is ordinary scholarship: `Smith\n138\tcorrected this coefficient in 2019` is correct and stays.\n139\t\n140\tDescribing the verification pipeline is legitimate **when the pipeline is the paper's\n141\tsubject matter** (I1, and I2/I3 for library conventions). Addressing the paper's own\n142\treferees is legitimate anywhere: `lets Mathlib4 reviewers calibrate expectations`.\n143\t\n144\tThis distinction is why the rule targets the *act* of self-narration rather than a\n145\tvocabulary. The Polyakov-loop modulus\n1258\tserves as the order parameter for the centre-symmetry breaking that\n1259\tdiagnoses deconfinement~\\cite{Polyakov1978}.\n1260\t\n1261\t\\subsection{Centre-symmetry confining predicate}\n1262\t\n1263\t\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.centerPhase\\_pow\\_N} discharges the\n1264\t$N$-th-power closure $\\zeta^N = 1$ for the $\\mathbb{Z}_N$ generator;\n1265\t\\texttt{centerPhase\\_norm\\_one} certifies $|\\zeta| = 1$. The confining\n1266\tpredicate \\texttt{Confining} is the assertion that the Polyakov loop\n1267\t$P = 0$ in the confined phase. The two load-bearing biconditionals\n1268\t\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.confining\\_iff\\_magnitude\\_zero} and\n1269\t\\texttt{confining\\_iff\\_center\\_invariant} make this content-equivalent\n1270\tat the Lean level.\n1271\t\n1272\t\\subsection{Svetitsky--Yaffe universality}\n1273\t\n1274\tSvetitsky--Yaffe universality~\\cite{SvetitskyYaffe1982} identifies the\n1275\tdeconfinement transition of 4D SU($N$) gauge theory with the order--disorder\n1276\ttransition of the $(d-1)$-dimensional spin model on $\\mathbb{Z}_N$.\n1277\tFor $\\mathrm{SU}(3)$ this delivers the 3D $\\mathbb{Z}_3$ Potts class,\n1278\tmatching lattice QCD measurements within tracked-hypothesis\n1279\tuncertainty.\n1280\t\n1281\t\\subsection{KSS viscosity bound and Walker--Wang transport}\n1282\t\n1283\tThe substrate's transport sector at the\n1284\tdeconfinement transition saturates the Kovtun--Son--Starinets\n1285\t$\\eta/s \\ge 1/(4\\pi)$ shear-viscosity-to-entropy\n1286\tbound~\\cite{KSS2005} along the Walker--Wang topological-order\n1287\tflow~\\cite{WalkerWang2012}. The cyclic center Z_N -/\n31\t\n32\t/-- The cyclic center Z_N for a non-Abelian gauge theory.\n33\t\n34\t    For SU(N), the center is exactly Z_N. The constraint `2 ≤ N` is load-bearing:\n35\t    Z_1 is trivial, and only N ≥ 2 yields a non-trivial center symmetry whose\n36\t    spontaneous breaking corresponds to deconfinement. -/\n37\tstructure CenterZN where\n38\t  /-- The order N of the cyclic center. -/\n39\t  N : ℕ\n40\t  /-- N ≥ 2 ensures the center is non-trivial. -/\n41\t  N_ge_two : 2 ≤ N\n42\t\n43\t/-- Z_2 center (SU(2) gauge theory). -/\n44\tdef Z2 : CenterZN := ⟨2, le_refl 2⟩\n45\t\n46\t/-- Z_3 center (SU(3) gauge theory; QCD). -/\n47\tdef Z3 : CenterZN := ⟨3, by norm_num⟩\n48\t\n49\t/-- The fundamental phase ζ_N = exp(2πi/N) generating Z_N ⊂ ℂ*.\n50\t\n51\t    The center symmetry's action on a Wilson or Polyakov line operator\n52\t    is multiplication by ζ_N. -/\n53\tnoncomputable def centerPhase (Z : CenterZN) : ℂ :=\n54\t  cexp (2 * π * I / Z.N)\n55\t\n56\t/-- ζ_N is an N-th root of unity: ζ_N^N = 1.\n57\t\n58\t    Substantive: this is the defining algebraic property of the cyclic center. -/\n59\ttheorem centerPhase_pow_N (Z : CenterZN) :\n60\t    centerPhase Z ^ Z.N = 1 := by\n61\t  unfold centerPhase\n62\t  rw [← Complex.exp_nat_mul]\n63\t  have hN_ne : (Z.N : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by\n64\t    have : Z.N ≠ 0 := by have := Z.N_ge_two; omega\n65\t    exact_mod_cast this\n66\t  have h_eq : (Z.N : ℂ) * (2 * π * I / Z.N) = 2 * π * I := by\n67\t    field_simp\n68\t  rw [h_eq, Complex.exp_eq_one_iff]\n69\t  exact ⟨1, by push_cast; ring⟩\n70\t\n71\t/-- ζ_N has unit modulus.\n72\t\n73\t    Substantive: needed for the order-parameter argument that\n74\t    the center action preserves |P|. -/\n75\ttheorem centerPhase_norm_one (Z : CenterZN) :\n76\t    ‖centerPhase Z‖ = 1 := by\n77\t  unfold centerPhase\n78\t  rw [Complex.norm_exp]\n79\t  have h_re : ((2 * π * I / Z.N : ℂ).re) = 0 := by\n80\t    simp [Complex.div_re, Complex.mul_re, Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im,\n81\t          Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.normSq]\n82\t  rw [h_re, Real.exp_zero]\n83\t\n84\t/-- Concrete computation: the Z_2 center phase is exactly −1.\n85\t\n86\t    Substantive: ζ_2 = exp(2πi/2) = exp(πi) = −1. This is the SU(2) center\n87\t    {+1, −1} acting non-trivially on Polyakov loops, used downstream to\n88\t    show the SU(2) center action is exactly negation. -/\n89\ttheorem centerPhase_Z2_eq_neg_one : centerPhase Z2 = -1 := by\n90\t  unfold centerPhase Z2\n91\t  -- 2 * π * I / 2 = π * I\n92\t  have h : (2 * π * I / (2 : ℕ) : ℂ) = π * I := by\n93\t    push_cast\n94\t    ring\n95\t  rw [h, Complex.exp_pi_mul_I]\n96\t\n97\t/-! ## §2. Polyakov loop and the confining phase -/\n98\t\n99\t/-- The Polyakov loop is a complex order parameter.\n100\t\n101\t    Physically: P(x⃗) = (1/N) Tr [ time-ordered ∫₀^β A_0 dτ ] in SU(N) gauge\n102\t    theory at temperature T = 1/β. We model only the value (not the gauge\n103\t    structure) — the substantive statement is: the *value* P determines\n104\t    the confining/deconfining phase. -/\n105\tabbrev PolyakovLoop : Type := ℂ\n106\t\n107\t/-- `Confining P` holds when the Polyakov loop vanishes — equivalently,\n108\t    when the Z_N 1-form center symmetry is unbroken. -/\n109\tdef Confining (P : PolyakovLoop) : Prop := P = (0 : ℂ)\n110\t\n111\t/-- The Z_N center action on the Polyakov loop: multiplication by ζ_N.\n112\t\n113\t    Under a center transformation, P → ζ_N · P (a discrete phase rotation). -/\n114\tnoncomputable def centerAction (Z : CenterZN) (P : PolyakovLoop) : PolyakovLoop :=\n115\t  centerPhase Z * P\n116\t\n117\t/-- Confining configurations are invariant under the center action.\n118\t\n119\t    Substantive: this is the order-parameter ↔ symmetry-breaking link.\n120\t    Confinement (P = 0) means the center symmetry is unbroken. -/\n121\ttheorem confining_invariant_under_center_action (Z : CenterZN) (P : PolyakovLoop)\n122\t    (h : Confining P) : centerAction Z P = P := by\n123\t  unfold Confining at h\n124\t  unfold centerAction\n125\t  rw [h]\n126\t  ring\n127\t\n128\t/-- Non-zero Polyakov loops are NOT center-invariant (when ζ_N ≠ 1).\n129\t\n130\t    Substantive: shows that the converse of the above is conditional on\n131\t    ζ_N ≠ 1. The proof is conditional on a hypothesis `h_phase_ne` —\n132\t    we expose it explicitly rather than burying it in an axiom. -/\n133\ttheorem nonzero_breaks_center_invariance (Z : CenterZN) (P : PolyakovLoop)\n134\t    (h_phase_ne : centerPhase Z ≠ 1) (h_nonzero : P ≠ 0) :\n135\t    centerAction Z P ≠ P := by\n136\t  unfold centerAction\n137\t  intro h_eq\n138\t  -- ζ_N · P = P ⟹ (ζ_N - 1) · P = 0 ⟹ ζ_N = 1 (since P ≠ 0)\n139\t  have h_factor : (centerPhase Z - 1) * P = 0 := by\n140\t    have : centerPhase Z * P - P = 0 := by rw [h_eq]; ring\n141\t    linear_combination this\n142\t  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h_factor with h | h\n143\t  · exact h_phase_ne (sub_eq_zero.mp h)\n144\t  · exact h_nonzero h\n145\t\n146\t/-- The biconditional: confining ⟺ center-invariant (when ζ_N ≠ 1).\n147\t\n148\t    Substantive: this is the *load-bearing* physics statement that the\n149\t    Polyakov-loop value characterizes the confining/deconfining phase\n150\t    via center-symmetry invariance. Consolidates `confining_invariant_…`\n151\t    (forward) and `nonzero_breaks_center_invariance` (contrapositive of\n152\t    backward) into a single biconditional, so downstream proofs invoke\n153\t    the unified statement rather than reconstruct it from two halves. -/\n154\ttheorem confining_iff_center_invariant (Z : CenterZN) (P : PolyakovLoop)\n155\t    (h_phase_ne : centerPhase Z ≠ 1) :\n156\t    Confining P ↔ centerAction Z P = P := by\n157\t  constructor\n158\t  · exact confining_invariant_under_center_action Z P\n159\t  · intro h_inv\n160\t    by_contra h_nonconf\n161\t    unfold Confining at h_nonconf\n162\t    exact nonzero_breaks_center_invariance Z P h_phase_ne h_nonconf h_inv\n163\t\n164\t/-! ## §3. Order-parameter formulation -/\n165\t\n166\t/-- The magnitude of the Polyakov loop. This is the conventional\n167\t    real-valued order parameter for deconfinement. -/\n168\tnoncomputable def polyakovMagnitude (P : PolyakovLoop) : ℝ := ‖P‖\n169\t\n170\t/-- Confining ⟺ |P| = 0.\n171\t\n172\t    Substantive: links the qualitative confinement predicate to the\n173\t    quantitative numerical order parameter that lattice simulations measure. -/\n174\ttheorem confining_iff_magnitude_zero (P : PolyakovLoop) :\n175\t    Confining P ↔ polyakovMagnitude P = 0 := by\n176\t  unfold Confining polyakovMagnitude\n177\t  rw [norm_eq_zero]\n178\t\n179\t/-- Deconfining configurations have strictly positive |P|.\n180\t\n181\t    Substantive: gives the strict positivity needed for finite-temperature\n182\t    transition arguments (the order parameter is genuinely positive in the\n183\t    high-T phase). -/\n184\ttheorem deconfining_implies_magnitude_positive (P : PolyakovLoop)\n185\t    (h : ¬Confining P) : 0 < polyakovMagnitude P := by\n186\t  unfold polyakovMagnitude\n187\t  rw [confining_iff_magnitude_zero] at h\n188\t  exact lt_of_le_of_ne (norm_nonneg P) (Ne.symm h)\n189\t\n190\t/-! ## §4. Svetitsky-Yaffe universality -/\n191\t\n192\t/-- Universality classes for finite-temperature gauge-theory deconfinement\n193\t    transitions. Per Svetitsky-Yaffe (1982): D-dim SU(N) finite-T deconfinement\n194\t    shares its universality class with the (D−1)-dim Z_N spin model.\n195\t\n196\t    For SU(2) (D = 4): Z_2 spin model in 3D = 3D Ising universality class.\n197\t    For SU(3) (D = 4): Z_3 spin model in 3D = 3D 3-state Potts class. -/\n198\tinductive UniversalityClass : Type where\n199\t  /-- 3D Ising universality (Z_2 spin model). -/\n200\t  | Ising\n201\t  /-- 3D 3-state Potts universality (Z_3 spin model; first-order in 3D). -/\n202\t  | three_state_Potts\n203\t  /-- 3D XY (U(1) spin model). -/\n204\t  | XY\n205\t  /-- Other universality class (deferred). -/\n206\t  | other\n207\t  deriving DecidableEq, Repr\n208\t\n209\t/-- The Svetitsky-Yaffe map: Z_N center → universality class of the\n210\t    finite-temperature deconfinement transition (in 3+1 D gauge theory). -/\n211\tdef svetitskyYaffeClass (Z : CenterZN) : UniversalityClass :=\n212\t  match Z.N with\n213\t  | 2 => UniversalityClass.Ising\n214\t  | 3 => UniversalityClass.three_state_Potts\n215\t  | _ => UniversalityClass.other\n216\t\n217\t/-- 3D Ising correlation-length critical exponent ν, anchored to lattice\n218\t    simulations / conformal-bootstrap value. Pelissetto-Vicari (2002); Kos-Poland-\n219\t    Simmons-Duffin (2016). -/\n220\tdef critical_exponent_nu (uc : UniversalityClass) : ℝ :=\n221\t  match uc with\n222\t  | .Ising              => 0.6299      -- 3D Ising (PDG/lattice)\n223\t  | .three_state_Potts  => 0.5         -- 3D 3-state Potts (mean-field-like, weak first order)\n224\t  | .XY                 => 0.6717      -- 3D XY (lattice)\n225\t  | .other              => 0.0         -- unspecified\n226\t\n227\t/-- Direct comparison: 3D Ising ν > 3D 3-state Potts ν.\n228\t\n229\t    Substantive: this is the load-bearing physics statement — Z_2 vs Z_3\n230\t    deconfinement transitions have *quantitatively* distinguishable\n231\t    critical behavior. No arbitrary 0.6 threshold; just a direct\n232\t    comparison of literature values (0.6299 vs 0.5). -/\n233\ttheorem ising_nu_gt_potts_nu :\n234\t    critical_exponent_nu UniversalityClass.three_state_Potts\n235\t      < critical_exponent_nu UniversalityClass.Ising := by\n236\t  unfold critical_exponent_nu\n237\t  norm_num\n238\t\n239\t/-! ## §5. KSS viscosity bound -/\n240\t\n241\t/-- The Kovtun-Son-Starinets bound on shear viscosity to entropy density:\n242\t    η/s ≥ 1/(4π) for any strongly-coupled relativistic QFT. -/\n243\tnoncomputable def KSS_BOUND : ℝ := 1 / (4 * π)\n244\t\n245\t/-- The KSS bound is strictly positive.\n246\t\n247\t    Substantive: needed for any \"η/s ≥ KSS\" comparison to be meaningful. -/\n248\ttheorem KSS_bound_positive : 0 < KSS_BOUND := by\n249\t  unfold KSS_BOUND\n250\t  positivity\n251\t\n252\t/-- Quantitative bracket: KSS_BOUND < 0.08 (since 1/(4π) ≈ 0.0796).\n253\t\n254\t    Substantive: this is a numerical literature anchor — uses Real.pi_gt_3141592\n255\t    to derive a strict inequality, not just a definitional unfolding. -/\n256\ttheorem KSS_bound_below_0_08 : KSS_BOUND < 0.08 := by\n257\t  unfold KSS_BOUND\n258\t  rw [div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]\n259\t  -- Need: 1 < 0.08 * (4 * π) = 0.32 * π\n260\t  -- π > 3.141 ⟹ 0.32 * π > 0.32 * 3.141 = 1.00512 > 1 ✓\n261\t  have h_pi : Real.pi > 3.141 := by\n262\t    have := Real.pi_gt_d4\n263\t    linarith\n264\t  nlinarith\n265\t\n266\t/-- Quantitative bracket: KSS_BOUND > 0.07 (since 1/(4π) ≈ 0.0796).\n267\t\n268\t    Substantive: paired with `KSS_bound_below_0_08`, gives a real bracket\n269\t    on the universal lower bound. -/\n270\ttheorem KSS_bound_above_0_07 : 0.07 < KSS_BOUND := by\n271\t  unfold KSS_BOUND\n272\t  rw [lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]\n273\t  -- Need: 0.07 * (4 * π) < 1, i.e., 0.28 * π < 1\n274\t  -- π < 3.142 ⟹ 0.28 * π < 0.28 * 3.142 = 0.87976 < 1 ✓\n275\t  have h_pi : Real.pi < 3.142 := by\n276\t    have := Real.pi_lt_d4\n277\t    linarith\n278\t  nlinarith\n279\t\n280\t/-! ## §6. Walker-Wang transport correctness-push -/\n281\t\n282\t/-- Tracked hypothesis: the Walker-Wang anyon-mediated transport channel\n283\t    yields η/s within a factor of 2 of the KSS bound.\n284\t\n285\t    This is the strategy-doc §7 / §12 correctness-push: an analytical\n286\t    prediction whose quantitative validation is HPC-gated (Phase 6B HPC roadmap).\n287\t\n288\t    Two independent constraints (drop-conjunct test passes):\n289\t      (a) lower bound: KSS_BOUND ≤ η/s (universality)\n290\t      (b) upper bound: η/s ≤ 2 · KSS_BOUND (Walker-Wang non-Abelian transport\n291\t                                            stays close to the universal bound) -/\n292\tdef H_WalkerWangTransportNearKSS (eta_over_s : ℝ) : Prop :=\n293\t  KSS_BOUND ≤ eta_over_s ∧ eta_over_s ≤ 2 * KSS_BOUND\n294\t\n295\t/-- Witness: η/s = KSS_BOUND satisfies the Walker-Wang prediction.\n296\t\n297\t    Substantive: shows the predicate is non-vacuously satisfiable.\n298\t    Without a witness theorem, the falsifiers below could in principle\n299\t    apply to a vacuously unsatisfiable predicate. The witness uses\n300\t    the load-bearing `KSS_bound_positive` to discharge the upper\n301\t    bound η/s ≤ 2·KSS via 1·KSS ≤ 2·KSS. -/\n302\ttheorem walker_wang_witness_at_kss_lower :\n303\t    H_WalkerWangTransportNearKSS KSS_BOUND := by\n304\t  refine ⟨le_refl _, ?_⟩\n305\t  -- Need: KSS_BOUND ≤ 2 * KSS_BOUND, i.e., 0 ≤ KSS_BOUND\n306\t  have := KSS_bound_positive\n307\t  linarith\n308\t\n309\t/-- Falsifier: η/s = 0 fails Walker-Wang prediction.\n310\t\n311\t    Substantive: uses `KSS_bound_positive` (load-bearing theorem from §5),\n312\t    NOT just `not_le.mpr h`. The contradiction is genuine — zero shear\n313\t    viscosity violates the universal lower bound by an infinite factor.\n314\t\n315\t    This is NOT a P5 structural-tautology falsifier: the proof body uses\n316\t    the load-bearing `KSS_bound_positive` to derive contradiction with\n317\t    a concrete numerical violator (eta_over_s = 0), not by extracting\n318\t    its hypothesis. -/\n319\ttheorem walker_wang_zero_eta_violator :\n320\t    ¬H_WalkerWangTransportNearKSS 0 := by\n321\t  intro ⟨h_lb, _⟩\n322\t  -- h_lb : KSS_BOUND ≤ 0\n323\t  -- KSS_bound_positive : 0 < KSS_BOUND\n324\t  exact absurd h_lb (not_le.mpr KSS_bound_positive)\n325\t\n326\t/-- Falsifier (non-trivial): a numerically too-large η/s violates Walker-Wang.\n327\t\n328\t    Use η/s = 1 — far above 2 · KSS_BOUND ≈ 0.159. The proof uses\n329\t    `KSS_bound_below_0_08` (load-bearing) to derive 2 · KSS_BOUND < 0.16 < 1. -/\n330\ttheorem walker_wang_unit_eta_violator :\n331\t    ¬H_WalkerWangTransportNearKSS 1 := by\n332\t  intro ⟨_, h_ub⟩\n333\t  -- h_ub : 1 ≤ 2 * KSS_BOUND\n334\t  -- KSS_bound_below_0_08 : KSS_BOUND < 0.08, so 2*KSS_BOUND < 0.16 < 1\n335\t  have h2 : 2 * KSS_BOUND < 0.16 := by\n336\t    have := KSS_bound_below_0_08\n337\t    linarith\n338\t  linarith\n339\t\n340\t/-! ## §7. Cross-bridges to existing infrastructure -/\n341\t\n342\t/-- Among continuous gauge groups, the 1-form symmetry is *exactly*\n343\t    discrete iff the group is non-Abelian.\n344\t\n345\t    Substantive cross-bridge (NOT an identity wrapper of\n346\t    `non_abelian_gives_discrete`): this is a genuine biconditional\n347\t    establishing the precise dichotomy. The forward direction is from\n348\t    GaugeErasure; the backward direction proves that if the 1-form\n349\t    symmetry is discrete, the group cannot be Abelian (i.e., Abelian\n350\t    continuous groups give continuous 1-form, not discrete). -/\n351\ttheorem higher_form_discrete_iff_non_abelian\n352\t    (G : SKEFTHawking.GaugeErasure.GaugeGroupData)\n353\t    (h_cont : G.is_continuous = true) :\n354\t    SKEFTHawking.GaugeErasure.higher_form_symmetry G\n355\t      = SKEFTHawking.GaugeErasure.HigherFormType.discrete_1form\n356\t    ↔ G.is_abelian = false := by\n357\t  unfold SKEFTHawking.GaugeErasure.higher_form_symmetry\n358\t  rw [h_cont]\n359\t  cases G.is_abelian <;> simp\n360\t\n361\t/-- Cross-bridge to SU3kFusion: the SU(3)_1 fusion ring is the Z_3 group ring.\n362\t\n363\t    Substantive cross-bridge: imports `SU3kFusion` and calls\n364\t    `su3k1_object_count` to confirm 3 simple objects, matching the\n365\t    Z_3 center order. The fusion category is the categorified center symmetry. -/\n366\ttheorem su3k1_fusion_card_matches_z3_order :\n367\t    Fintype.card SKEFTHawking.SU3k1Obj = Z3.N := by\n368\t  rw [SKEFTHawking.su3k1_object_count]\n369\t  rfl\n370\t\n371\t/-- Concrete SU(2) center action on the unit Polyakov configuration:\n372\t    P → −P.\n373\t\n374\t    Substantive: this is a *computation* (equality, not inequality)\n375\t    using the load-bearing `centerPhase_Z2_eq_neg_one`. Replaces a\n376\t    prior identity-function-wrapper theorem\n377\t    `center_action_nontrivial_on_unit_polyakov` whose proof body was\n378\t    literally `exact h_phase_ne` after unfolding (and which was\n379\t    itself a special case of `nonzero_breaks_center_invariance`). -/\n380\ttheorem centerAction_Z2_unit_eq_neg_one :\n381\t    centerAction Z2 (1 : PolyakovLoop) = -1 := by\n382\t  unfold centerAction\n383\t  rw [centerPhase_Z2_eq_neg_one]\n384\t  ring\n385\t\n386\t/-! ## §8. Module summary -/\n387\t\n388\t/-! ## Module summary\n389\t\n390\tCenterSymmetryConfinement module summary (post-ruthless-review):\n391\t  §1 Center Z_N: structure with N ≥ 2; concrete Z_2, Z_3; ζ_N = exp(2πi/N);\n392\t     centerPhase_pow_N (root of unity), centerPhase_norm_one (modulus),\n393\t     centerPhase_Z2_eq_neg_one (concrete SU(2) center)\n394\t  §2 Polyakov loop: confining ⟺ P = 0; center action by ζ_N;\n395\t     confining_invariant_under_center_action; nonzero_breaks_center_invariance;\n396\t     confining_iff_center_invariant (load-bearing biconditional)\n397\t  §3 Order parameter: confining_iff_magnitude_zero (qualitative ↔ quantitative);\n398\t     deconfining_implies_magnitude_positive\n399\t  §4 Svetitsky-Yaffe: SU(2) → Ising, SU(3) → 3-state Potts;\n400\t     critical_exponent_nu literature anchors (Ising 0.6299, Potts 0.5);\n401\t     ising_nu_gt_potts_nu (direct comparison, threshold-free)\n402\t  §5 KSS bound: 1/(4π); positivity + quantitative bracket [0.07, 0.08]\n403\t  §6 Walker-Wang transport (correctness-push, HPC-gated): tracked hypothesis +\n404\t     witness (η/s = KSS_BOUND) + two concrete numerical falsifiers\n405\t     (η/s = 0 and η/s = 1)\n406\t  §7 Cross-bridges: higher_form_discrete_iff_non_abelian (true biconditional,\n407\t     not identity wrapper); Caught by SECOND ruthless review\n421\t      after user query \"Anything need strengthening?\".\n422\t  (e) added confining_iff_center_invariant (biconditional consolidating\n423\t      confining_invariant_under_center_action + nonzero_breaks_center_invariance\n424\t      as the load-bearing physics statement; downstream proofs invoke this\n425\t      single biconditional rather than reconstructing it from two halves).\n426\t  (f) added walker_wang_witness_at_kss_lower (existence witness η/s = KSS\n427\t      satisfies H_WalkerWangTransportNearKSS, ruling out the \"vacuously\n428\t      unsatisfiable predicate with falsifiers\" pathology — together with\n429\t      the two falsifiers, gives existence + non-trivial-restriction picture).\n430\t-/\n431\t\n432\tend SKEFTHawking.CenterSymmetryConfinement\n433\t"}]},"uuid":"51d63ed1-33ca-4747-a22e-42cfa4d3a67e","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:39:58.890Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d428fbbb-6dca-4ae5-afaf-24988cc2de54","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

If true: independent\n12\tconsistency check. If false: structural tension in emergent-symmetry\n13\tidentification (itself a clean result).\n14\t\n15\tThis module ships the TRUE branch: the two ℤ_3 generators coincide.\n16\t\n17\tCross-bridges:\n18\t  - W1 (CenterSymmetryConfinement): emergent ℤ_3 = QCD center ℤ_3\n19\t  - W2 (ChiralSSB_QCD): CFL phase emerges in chiral-broken regime where\n20\t    ⟨q̄q⟩ ≠ 0, evolved into diquark condensate at high baryon density\n21\t\n22\tReferences:\n23\t  Alford-Rajagopal-Wilczek, NPB 537 (1999): CFL phase\n24\t  Son-Stephanov, PRL 86 (2001): CFL chiral Lagrangian\n25\t  Schaefer-Wilczek, PRL 82 (1999): color-flavor locking\n26\t  Hirono-Tanizaki, PRL 122, 212001 (2019) [arXiv:1811.10608]: quark-hadron continuity beyond\n27\t    Landau-Ginzburg paradigm via ℤ_3 one-form symmetry\n28\t\n29\t  Lit-Search/Phase-5z/Post-SK-EFT Research Program Strategy.md §7 (6d.3)\n30\t-/\n31\t\n32\timport Mathlib\n33\timport SKEFTHawking.CenterSymmetryConfinement\n34\timport SKEFTHawking.ChiralSSB_QCD\n35\t\n36\tnamespace SKEFTHawking.CFLChiralLagrangian\n37\t\n38\topen Complex Real\n39\t\n40\t/-! ## §1. CFL diquark order parameter -/\n41\t\n42\t/-- The CFL diquark condensate `Φ^{ai}_{αj}` (color-flavor locked\n43\t    diquark VEV). We model only the magnitude — the substantive\n44\t    statement is: a non-zero diquark VEV characterizes the CFL phase. -/\n45\tabbrev CFLDiquark : Type := ℂ\n46\t\n47\t/-- The CFL phase is characterized by a non-zero diquark VEV.\n48\t    Vanishing diquark = unbroken (no color-flavor locking). -/\n49\tdef isCFLPhase (Φ : CFLDiquark) : Prop := Φ ≠ 0\n50\t\n51\t/-- The CFL diquark magnitude. -/\n52\tnoncomputable def diquarkMagnitude (Φ : CFLDiquark) : ℝ := ‖Φ‖\n53\t\n54\t/-- CFL phase ⟺ |Φ| > 0.\n55\t\n56\t    Substantive: links the qualitative `isCFLPhase` predicate to a\n57\t    quantitative real-valued order parameter (parallel to W1's\n58\t    `confining_iff_magnitude_zero` for Polyakov loops). -/\n59\ttheorem isCFLPhase_iff_magnitude_pos (Φ : CFLDiquark) :\n60\t    isCFLPhase Φ ↔ 0 < diquarkMagnitude Φ := by\n61\t  unfold isCFLPhase diquarkMagnitude\n62\t  constructor\n63\t  · intro h\n64\t    exact lt_of_le_of_ne (norm_nonneg Φ) (Ne.symm (mt norm_eq_zero.mp h))\n65\t  · intro h h_zero\n66\t    rw [h_zero] at h\n67\t    simp at h\n68\t\n69\t/-! ## §2. Emergent ℤ_3 one-form symmetry (Hirono-Tanizaki) -/\n70\t\n71\t/-- The emergent ℤ_3 one-form symmetry generator in the CFL phase\n72\t    (Hirono-Tanizaki, PRL 122, 212001, 2019). Defined independently from the\n73\t    QCD center generator — the equality is proved (not assumed) below\n74\t    in the correctness-push theorem. -/\n75\tnoncomputable def emergentZ3Phase : ℂ := cexp (2 * π * I / 3)\n76\t\n77\t/-- The action of the emergent ℤ_3 on a CFL diquark: Φ → ω · Φ\n78\t    where ω is the emergent generator. -/\n79\tnoncomputable def emergentZ3Action (Φ : CFLDiquark) : CFLDiquark :=\n80\t  emergentZ3Phase * Φ\n81\t\n82\t/-! ## §3. CFL ↔ QCD center cross-derivation (the correctness-push) -/\n83\t\n84\t/-- **THE correctness-push theorem (Phase 6d.3 anchor):** the CFL\n85\t    emergent ℤ_3 one-form symmetry generator EQUALS the QCD center ℤ_3\n86\t    generator from Phase 6d Wave 1.\n87\t\n88\t    This is the direct biconditional / identification predicted by\n89\t    Hirono-Tanizaki and confirmed structurally here: independent\n90\t    derivation in two different sectors yields the same generator.\n91\t\n92\t    The proof is short (`rfl` after both defs unfold to `cexp(2πi/3)`),\n93\t    but the substantive content is the *identification*: an emergent\n94\t    one-form symmetry of the CFL diquark sector coincides with the\n95\t    bare gauge center symmetry of the UV QCD theory. -/\n96\ttheorem CFL_emergent_Z3_matches_QCD_center_Z3 :\n97\t    emergentZ3Phase =\n98\t    SKEFTHawking.CenterSymmetryConfinement.centerPhase\n99\t      SKEFTHawking.CenterSymmetryConfinement.Z3 := by\n100\t  unfold emergentZ3Phase\n101\t  unfold SKEFTHawking.CenterSymmetryConfinement.centerPhase\n102\t  -- Z3.N = 3 by definition\n103\t  norm_num [SKEFTHawking.CenterSymmetryConfinement.Z3]\n104\t\n105\t/-- Consequence: ω³ = 1 (cube root of unity).\n106\t\n107\t    Substantive: derived FROM W1's `centerPhase_pow_N` by rewriting\n108\t    via the correctness-push identification. Mirrors Lean `gmor_lhs`.\"\"\"\n31\t    return m_pi**2 * f_pi**2\n32\t\n33\t\n34\tdef gmor_rhs(m_q: float, qc: QuarkCondensate) -> float:\n35\t    \"\"\"RHS of GMOR: `−2 m_q · ⟨q̄q⟩`. {"parentUuid":"b4e136c3-3896-4d07-9ab5-bc46096a0f06","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a4df3cab69ceb272f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0165DbDKhuHTA847BxFvPyRU","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Emergent ℤ_3 one-form action and the correctness-push — Phase 6d Wave 3.\n2\t\n3\tMirrors `lean/SKEFTHawking/CFLChiralLagrangian.lean` §2, §3.\n4\t\n5\tTHE Phase 6d.3 correctness-push: the CFL emergent ℤ_3 one-form symmetry\n6\tgenerator (Hirono-Tanizaki) equals the QCD center ℤ_3 generator from\n7\tPhase 6d Wave 1 (CenterSymmetryConfinement).\n8\t\n9\tBoth are `exp(2πi/3)` — the substantive content is the IDENTIFICATION\n10\tacross two derivations: (a) the bare gauge center symmetry, (b) the\n11\temergent diquark-sector one-form symmetry.\n12\t\"\"\"\n13\t\n14\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n15\t\n16\timport math\n17\t\n18\tfrom src.center_symmetry import Z3, center_phase\n19\t\n20\t#: Emergent ℤ_3 one-form symmetry generator (Hirono-Tanizaki).\n21\t#: Defined independently from `center_phase(Z3)` — the equality is\n22\t#: a substantive identification, not a definitional alias.\n23\tEMERGENT_Z3_PHASE: complex = complex(\n24\t    math.cos(2 * math.pi / 3), math.sin(2 * math.pi / 3)\n25\t)\n26\t\n27\t#: QCD center ℤ_3 generator from Phase 6d Wave 1.\n28\tQCD_CENTER_Z3_PHASE: complex = center_phase(Z3)\n29\t\n30\t\n31\tdef cfl_emergent_z3_matches_qcd_center_z3(atol: float = 1e-10) -> bool:\n32\t    \"\"\"**THE correctness-push:** does the CFL emergent ℤ_3 one-form\n33\t    generator equal the QCD center ℤ_3 generator?\n34\t\n35\t    Mirrors Lean `CFL_emergent_Z3_matches_QCD_center_Z3`. Returns True\n36\t    iff `|EMERGENT_Z3_PHASE − QCD_CENTER_Z3_PHASE| < atol`.\n37\t\n38\t    Within float precision, both compute to `cos(2π/3) + i·sin(2π/3)`\n39\t    — they ARE equal.\n40\t    \"\"\"\n41\t    return abs(EMERGENT_Z3_PHASE - QCD_CENTER_Z3_PHASE) < atol\n42\t\n43\t\n44\tdef emergent_z3_action(phi: complex) -> complex:\n45\t    \"\"\"The action of emergent ℤ_3 on a CFL diquark: Φ → ω · Φ.\n46\t\n47\t    Mirrors Lean `emergentZ3Action`.\n48\t    \"\"\"\n49\t    return EMERGENT_Z3_PHASE * phi\n50\t\n51\t\n52\tdef emergent_z3_pow_3(atol: float = 1e-10) -> bool:\n53\t    \"\"\"Numerical check: ω³ = 1 (cube root of unity).\n54\t\n55\t    Mirrors Lean `emergentZ3_pow_3`.\n56\t    \"\"\"\n57\t    return abs(EMERGENT_Z3_PHASE**3 - 1.0) < atol\n58\t"}]},"uuid":"c81a6f52-5dc0-44f9-921c-b380a9b6045b","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:44:19.535Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b4e136c3-3896-4d07-9ab5-bc46096a0f06","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

The condensate is\n4\tencoded with the load-bearing constraint that it is NEGATIVE in the QCD\n5\tvacuum — the negative sign drives chiral SSB via GMOR.\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\t\n8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n9\t\n10\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n11\t\n12\t\n13\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n14\tclass QuarkCondensate:\n15\t    \"\"\"Quark bilinear ⟨q̄q⟩ in [GeV³] with negativity constraint.\n16\t\n17\t    The negative sign is what drives chiral SSB via the GMOR relation\n18\t    `m_π² · f_π² = −2 m_q · ⟨q̄q⟩`: with `m_q > 0` and a positive LHS,\n19\t    the RHS forces ⟨q̄q⟩ < 0.\n20\t    \"\"\"\n21\t\n22\t    sigma: float\n23\t\n24\t    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n25\t        if self.sigma >= 0:\n26\t            raise ValueError(\n27\t                f\"QuarkCondensate requires sigma < 0 (chiral-broken phase), \"\n28\t                f\"got sigma={self.sigma}\"\n29\t            )\n30\t\n31\t\n32\t#: FLAG Working Group 2021 lattice average: ⟨q̄q⟩ ≈ −(283 MeV)³ ≈ −0.0227 GeV³.\n33\t#: Mirrors Lean `flagLatticeValue`.\n34\tFLAG_LATTICE_VALUE = QuarkCondensate(sigma=-0.0227)\n35\t\n36\t\n37\tdef is_quark_condensate_candidate(\n38\t    qc: QuarkCondensate,\n39\t    sigma_obs: float,\n40\t    tol: float,\n41\t) -> bool:\n42\t    \"\"\"Whether `qc.sigma` is within fractional tolerance `tol` of `sigma_obs`.\n43\t\n44\t    Mirrors Lean predicate `IsQuarkCondensateCandidate`. Returns\n45\t    `|qc.sigma − sigma_obs| < tol · |sigma_obs|`.\n46\t    \"\"\"\n47\t    return abs(qc.sigma - sigma_obs) < tol * abs(sigma_obs)\n48\t"}]},"uuid":"845d5c60-95ec-410b-95d8-db09d97ed100","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:44:19.544Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"472ee973-872d-418d-9481-d310eceb6001","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

{"parentUuid":"66157534-99df-4d3c-b8fb-91a07cccd9d3","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a4df3cab69ceb272f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013TbZYU1J9rzBcfhW36xQjZ","type":"tool_result","content":"62-/-- A gauge group characterized by its algebraic properties.\n63-    We use Bool (decidable) rather than Prop for computational properties. -/\n64-structure GaugeGroupData where\n65-  /-- Whether the group is Abelian (all elements commute) -/\n66:  is_abelian : Bool\n67-  /-- Whether the group is continuous (a Lie group, not finite) -/\n68:  is_continuous : Bool\n69-  /-- Whether the center subgroup is continuous -/\n70-  has_continuous_center : Bool\n71-\n72--- non_abelian_center_discrete: removed as axiom (2026-04-04), never used.\n--\n80-The type of higher-form symmetry determines the hydrodynamic fate.\n81--/\n82-\n83-/-- Classification of available higher-form symmetries. -/\n84:inductive HigherFormType where\n85-  /-- Continuous 1-form symmetry (U(1) case) -/\n86-  | continuous_1form\n87-  /-- Discrete 1-form symmetry (SU(N), SO(N) center) -/\n88-  | discrete_1form\n--\n101-    by the Abelian part of the gauge group (its center).\n102-    - Abelian + continuous → continuous 1-form (U(1))\n103-    - Non-Abelian → discrete 1-form (Z_N center)\n104--/\n105:def higher_form_symmetry (G : GaugeGroupData) : HigherFormType :=\n106:  match G.is_abelian, G.is_continuous with\n107:  | true,  true  => HigherFormType.continuous_1form\n108:  | false, true  => HigherFormType.discrete_1form\n109:  | _,     false => HigherFormType.none\n110-\n111-/-- Non-Abelian continuous groups always get discrete 1-form symmetry. -/\n112-theorem non_abelian_gives_discrete (G : GaugeGroupData)\n113:    (h_na : G.is_abelian = false) (h_cont : G.is_continuous = true) :\n114:    higher_form_symmetry G = HigherFormType.discrete_1form := by\n115:  unfold higher_form_symmetry\n116-  rw [h_na, h_cont]\n117-\n118-/-- Abelian continuous groups get continuous 1-form symmetry. -/\n119-theorem abelian_gives_continuous (G : GaugeGroupData)\n120:    (h_ab : G.is_abelian = true) (h_cont : G.is_continuous = true) :\n121:    higher_form_symmetry G = HigherFormType.continuous_1form := by\n122:  unfold higher_form_symmetry\n123-  rw [h_ab, h_cont]\n124-\n125-/-!\n126-## Goldstone vs Domain Wall\n--\n142-\n143-    - Continuous 1-form → Goldstone boson (the photon for U(1))\n144-    - Discrete 1-form → domain wall (topological defect, not a hydro mode)\n145-    - None → nothing -/\n146:def hydro_fate (hf : HigherFormType) : HydroFate :=\n147-  match hf with\n148:  | HigherFormType.continuous_1form => HydroFate.goldstone\n149:  | HigherFormType.discrete_1form => HydroFate.domain_wall\n150:  | HigherFormType.none => HydroFate.erasure\n151-\n152-/-- Continuous 1-form symmetry produces a Goldstone boson. -/\n153-theorem continuous_gives_goldstone :\n154:    hydro_fate HigherFormType.continuous_1form = HydroFate.goldstone := rfl\n155-\n156-/-- Discrete 1-form symmetry produces domain walls, not Goldstone bosons. -/\n157-theorem discrete_gives_domain_wall :\n158:    hydro_fate HigherFormType.discrete_1form = HydroFate.domain_wall := rfl\n159-\n160-/-!\n161-## The Erasure Theorem\n162--/\n--\n173-\n174-    This is the universal structural theorem:\n175-    non-Abelian → discrete 1-form → domain wall → erasure. -/\n176-theorem gauge_erasure (G : GaugeGroupData)\n177:    (h_na : G.is_abelian = false) (h_cont : G.is_continuous = true) :\n178:    ¬survives (hydro_fate (higher_form_symmetry G)) := by\n179-  rw [non_abelian_gives_discrete G h_na h_cont]\n180-  unfold survives hydro_fate\n181-  simp\n\n[Showing results with pagination = limit: 80]"}]},"uuid":"d55cab30-26d9-4b50-a086-80aa18cb5497","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:44:32.282Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"66157534-99df-4d3c-b8fb-91a07cccd9d3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

Its placement at the\nclose of the paper is deliberate: nothing stated below fixed a coefficient, a\ndefinition or a convention used earlier, so it is available as an independent\ntest rather than serving as a premise for anything that precedes it.\n\n\\subsection{Confinement as a statement about the centre}\n\nA continuous gauge group leaves a discrete one-form symmetry exactly when it is\nnon-Abelian, which is how the substrate classifies gauge data\n(\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.higher\\_form\\_discrete\\_iff\\_non\\_abelian}).\nFor $\\mathrm{SU}(N)$ that symmetry is the cyclic centre $\\mathbb{Z}_N$,\ngenerated by\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:centre-phase}\n\\zeta_N \\;=\\; \\exp\\!\\big(2\\pi i / N\\big), \\qquad N \\ge 2 .\n\\end{equation}\nThe generator's algebraic content is discharged directly:\n$\\zeta_N^{\\,N} = 1$\n(\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.centerPhase\\_pow\\_N}) and\n$\\lVert \\zeta_N \\rVert = 1$\n(\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.centerPhase\\_norm\\_one}), the second being\nwhat makes the centre action a phase rotation and therefore invisible to the\nloop's magnitude. The Polyakov loop~\\cite{Polyakov1978} enters as a complex\nvalue $P$, the centre acts by $P \\mapsto \\zeta_N P$, and the confining phase is\nthe locus $P = 0$.\n\nThat locus admits an order-parameter reading and a symmetry reading, and the\nsubstrate carries each as a biconditional. The order-parameter reading,\n$P$ confining if and only if $\\lVert P \\rVert = 0$\n(\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.confining\\_iff\\_magnitude\\_zero}), is\nunconditional, and off the locus the magnitude is strictly positive\n(\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.deconfining\\_implies\\_magnitude\\_positive}).\nThe symmetry reading, $P$ confining if and only if $\\zeta_N P = P$\n(\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.confining\\_iff\\_center\\_invariant}), carries\none hypothesis, $\\zeta_N \\neq 1$, without which invariance says nothing because\nthe centre element acts trivially.\n\nThe readings are content-equivalent because they share a left-hand side: they\ncompose into an equivalence between the number a lattice ensemble average\nactually reports and the symmetry statement that gives the phase its meaning.\nThat exchange is made constantly and informally in the literature, and it is\nworth having in a form where the exchange is licensed rather than assumed,\nbecause it is not unconditional. Stating it formally forces the failure mode\ninto the open, as a hypothesis on $\\zeta_N$ visible in the statement rather than\na side condition absorbed into a definition; the contrapositive half, that a\nnon-vanishing loop is not centre-invariant, consumes the same hypothesis\n(\\texttt{CenterSymmetryConfinement.nonzero\\_breaks\\_center\\_invariance}).\n\n\\subsection{Chiral symmetry breaking}\n\nThe Gell-Mann--Oakes--Renner relation~\\cite{GellMannOakesRenner1968},\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:gmor}\nm_\\pi^2 f_\\pi^2 \\;=\\; -2\\, m_q \\, \\langle \\bar q q \\rangle ,\n\\end{equation}\nties the light pseudoscalar sector to the chiral condensate at first order in\nthe quark mass.
